label: <DEL> step in long sequences, plus copy-phase inputs k/w/n/z/s
explanation: Most of the activation (60% of mass) is on the <DEL> delimiter step. The rate there climbs steeply with sequence length: about 0.33 overall, 0.57 for L>=7 and 0.68 for L>=8, and it is close to silent at <DEL> for short sequences. The rest (about 37% of mass) is in the copy phase. It is concentrated on steps whose fed-back input is k, w, n, z or s, but these fire only about 22% of the time, and some of the strongest copy activations are on the first copy step (the first token fed back right after <DEL>). It is almost silent during the original phase (2.7% of mass) and never fires at t=0. Magnitude is largest at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences. The precision of both clauses is weak, so this is a coarse description, not a full one.
